channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Apple Watch shows the wrong hour after the clock change: the fix
item.description: Apple published a support note for watches whose Always On display stays one hour off after daylight saving time ends. The wrong hour only shows while your wrist is down.

item.title: WhatsApp is working on a new settings look for Android
item.description: WhatsApp is building a new design for its Android settings, with items grouped into rounded sections, according to WABetaInfo, which follows the app's test versions. WhatsApp hasn't announced it.

item.title: ChatGPT and Codex will draw from one usage allowance
item.description: OpenAI told Pro subscribers by email that their ChatGPT and Codex use will come out of the same allowance. It will also test putting the Work tab's features into normal chats with a small group of users in the coming weeks.

item.title: ChatGPT now limits paid accounts per device and payment card
item.description: OpenAI caps how many paid ChatGPT subscriptions can share one payment card or one device. Past the limit, new subscriptions can't be started and the app shows "Device limit reached".

item.title: iOS 27: Apple Intelligence takes up to 16 GB, and a workaround
item.description: People who updated to iOS 27 report that Apple Intelligence uses about 9 to 16 GB of iPhone storage, GSMArena writes. That includes phones in regions where the features aren't available, like the EU.

item.title: New Outlook's unified inbox now due by late November
item.description: Microsoft pushed back the rollout of the All Accounts view, which puts mail from all your accounts in one inbox, in the new Outlook for Windows. It now expects to finish by late November instead of late October.

item.title: Amazon stops Meta's Muse AI agent from buying on its site
item.description: Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse shopping agent from making purchases on Amazon, citing safety concerns, according to The Wall Street Journal. Walmart and Shopify have made deals with Meta to work with Muse instead.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Family: 2TB shared instead of 1TB each
item.description: Microsoft 365 Family and Premium now come with 2TB of OneDrive storage shared by up to six people, instead of 1TB for each person. The Family plan's price stays $13 a month.

item.title: OpenAI fixed a ChatGPT share-link flaw that exposed private chats
item.description: Researchers at the security firm Parameter showed that a booby-trapped ChatGPT share link could run their code in the signed-in session of whoever opened it and read that person's private chats. OpenAI fixed it by 26 October.

item.title: YouTube bug pops videos out of full screen and cuts the sound
item.description: YouTube users on Android and iPhone report on Reddit that videos jump from full screen into the mini-player on their own, and the audio stops. Sammy Fans says reports go back to early October.

item.title: Spotify reportedly plans paid AI remixes for early 2027
item.description: Spotify is working on an AI feature that turns songs into remixes or covers, aiming for early 2027, according to the Financial Times as reported by PCMag. Spotify hasn't announced it.

item.title: Gemini gets a new sparkling look on Android phones
item.description: Google is rolling out a new design for the Gemini overlay on Android, with glowing dots and a sparkle animation around the "Ask Gemini" box. It comes through the Google app, so it isn't limited to new Pixel phones.

item.title: A hidden text message can drop calls on Android phones
item.description: A bug in Android lets one specially made text message, which never shows in your inbox, crash the phone's calling service and cut off calls, including emergency calls.

item.title: 319 Chrome extensions secretly rerouted people's searches
item.description: Researchers at Socket found 319 Chrome extensions, installed 13.4 million times, that changed the default search engine and sent searches through their own servers.

item.title: Google AI Plus loses Gemini's Pro models on 13 November
item.description: From 13 November, Google AI Plus subscribers can no longer pick Gemini's Pro models in the Gemini app or in AI Mode in Search. The Flash models stay.

item.title: Apple Music on Android gets a new look
item.description: Apple Music 7.0 for Android brings Apple's Liquid Glass design: a black or white icon, a floating bottom bar and blue instead of red accents.

item.title: YouTube TV members can get 3 months of YouTube Premium free
item.description: YouTube TV subscribers in the US who have never had YouTube Premium or a Premium trial can get three months of it at no cost, through a code sent by email.

item.title: Rian Johnson's camera app gives iPhone photos a film look
item.description: Chromagraph Camera, made by director Rian Johnson with cinematographer Steve Yedlin, shoots RAW photos and processes them with the color and grain techniques Yedlin developed for their films.

item.title: Agoda's app adds an AI assistant that plans and books trips
item.description: Agoda's AI Assistant is now in its app in 21 markets, including the US, India, Australia, Japan, Singapore and the UAE, after a limited test that started in September. You can plan, compare and book in one chat.

item.title: Google is working on a fix for Pixel Watch battery drain
item.description: Google said on Reddit that it has identified the problem behind sudden battery drain on some Pixel Watches and is working on a fix. It didn't give a date, only "as soon as possible".

item.title: ChatGPT tightens answers on weapons for teens and on past attacks
item.description: OpenAI said ChatGPT will stop giving teen accounts practical information about weapons and security systems, even for harmless-looking questions. For everyone, it will give less detail about past mass attacks.

item.title: Gemini Notebook adds hundreds of free textbooks
item.description: Google opened a free catalog of hundreds of textbooks in Gemini Notebook, from OpenStax, the Open Textbook Library and India's S Chand Publishing. Once added, you can ask about chapters and get quizzes, flashcards and study guides.

item.title: Reddit will ask for an account to read most pages
item.description: Reddit plans to make most browsing need a login. The front page, and posts opened from Google or a shared link, should stay open; tests start outside the US in the coming months.

item.title: Gemini can now write and edit files right in the chat
item.description: The Gemini app can create, preview and edit Google Docs, Sheets, slides, PDFs and text files inside a chat, with a full-screen editor.

item.title: WhatsApp groups get four new catch-up features
item.description: WhatsApp is rolling out four features for group chats: pins that never expire, sharing recent messages with new members, a status only one group sees, and a filter for mentions and replies.

item.title: Samsung News shuts down on 21 December
item.description: Samsung is ending its Samsung News feed on 21 December 2026. Its widget stops updating, and Samsung hasn't named a replacement.

item.title: Samsung Wallet adds a Cash Card for cash back
item.description: Samsung Wallet in the US has a new virtual Cash Card that collects cash back from Rakuten deals and can send money to other Samsung Wallet users.

item.title: Windows 11 lets you choose what's in the right-click menu
item.description: Microsoft's optional preview update KB5127936 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2 adds a "Customize menu" option at the bottom of the right-click menu. You pick which commands and app add-ons show up.

item.title: Meta's new Style Sketch app plans outfits from your own clothes
item.description: Meta quietly released Style Sketch, an AI app that builds a virtual closet and suggests outfits from clothes you already own. It's out on iPhone and Android in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.

item.title: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro limits instead of cutting them
item.description: After complaints about a planned cut, OpenAI doubled the usage limits of all ChatGPT Pro tiers and Business Premium, starting 29 October.

item.title: Text your ChatGPT Dot from your messages app
item.description: ChatGPT Pro users in the US can now message their Dot, OpenAI's background assistant, through Google Messages (RCS) or iMessage, as a preview.

item.title: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook is here
item.description: The new MacBook Pro has a touch display and the iPhone's Dynamic Island: calls, music and AirDrop show at the top of the screen.

item.title: Chrome can now fill forms from your Gmail
item.description: Chrome can now fill forms from your Gmail: order numbers, tracking details and flight bookings, suggested as you type.

item.title: MacPaw's new Eney assistant asks before it acts on your Mac
item.description: MacPaw launched Eney, an AI assistant for Mac that suggests next steps, takes meeting notes without a bot joining the call, and works with Mail, Calendar and Reminders. It asks before it sends a message, changes an event or moves a file.

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon goes to security teams first
item.description: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, its new top Gemini model; for now only selected cyber-security teams can use it, with no date for everyone else.

item.title: Reddit's new For You feed
item.description: Reddit adds a For You feed with picks for you, rolling out worldwide.

item.title: TikTok's restaurant guide
item.description: TikTok launched Must Eat: restaurant tips from 40 million posts and comments (New York, LA and San Francisco first).

item.title: Your Discord chats could show up on Google
item.description: Public chats in big Discord servers can appear on Google from mid-December, word for word (without usernames or avatars).

item.title: ChatGPT can now read your iCloud Mail and Calendar
item.description: ChatGPT now works with iCloud Mail and Calendar: find an email, catch up on your inbox, move a meeting.

item.title: Netflix now comes with a T-Mobile plan
item.description: T-Mobile's new T-Mix plans include a streaming service: pick Netflix or Hulu (with ads), Apple TV, YouTube Premium Lite and more, from $55 a month.

item.title: iOS 27.2: watch 4 live games at once
item.description: iOS 27.2 is out: watch up to 4 live games at once in the Apple TV app (MLS, F1, Friday Night Baseball; subscription needed).

item.title: Instagram tests long videos
item.description: Instagram is testing long, horizontal videos called Features, US first.
